boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along the Vine Street, Cajon Street, Olive Avenue, Eureka Street, State Street, and Orange Street corridors in central Redlands.

cards.title: A.K. Smiley Public Library
cards.subtitle: Vine Street corridor, 125 W. Vine St.
cards.notes: Walk the Vine Street corridor to see the 1898 library and use its public collections, Heritage Room, or regular library services.
cards.short_summary: A historic public library with local-history resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The library says it was dedicated with Smiley Park in 1898 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
cards.access_notes: Library address and current operating hours are published by A.K. Smiley Public Library.

cards.title: Lincoln Memorial Shrine
cards.subtitle: Vine Street corridor, beside A.K. Smiley Public Library
cards.notes: Continue through Smiley Park to the Shrine and plan a daytime visit during its posted Tuesday–Sunday public hours.
cards.short_summary: A city-administered Lincoln-focused museum in Smiley Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies the Lincoln Memorial Shrine as one of the two museums overseen by the A.K. Smiley Public Library trustees.
cards.source_title: A.K. Smiley Public Library — City of Redlands
cards.access_notes: The City lists Shrine hours as Tuesday–Sunday, 1–5 p.m.; confirm before visiting.

cards.title: Redlands Historical Museum
cards.subtitle: Vine Street corridor, at A.K. Smiley Public Library
cards.notes: Use the Vine Street stop to connect a library visit with the city’s historical-museum program and local-history context.
cards.short_summary: A local-history museum administered with the public library.
cards.evidence_claim: The City states that A.K. Smiley Public Library oversees the Redlands Historical Museum.
cards.source_title: A.K. Smiley Public Library — City of Redlands
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s museum information for current public access details.

cards.title: Smiley Park
cards.subtitle: Vine Street corridor, around 125 W. Vine St.
cards.notes: Pause in the park between the library and Shrine to view the named public artworks recorded in the City’s inventory.
cards.short_summary: A civic park with documented public art beside library institutions.
cards.evidence_claim: The City public-art inventory places the Smiley Brothers Memorial and Mother and Child in Smiley Park at 125 W. Vine Street.
cards.source_title: City of Redlands Public Art Inventory
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public-art viewing does not require a museum reservation.

cards.title: Redlands Bowl
cards.subtitle: Eureka Street corridor, 168 S. Eureka St.
cards.notes: Take Eureka Street south from the park to photograph the amphitheater and check the music association’s current performance calendar.
cards.short_summary: A city amphitheater associated with public music and theater.
cards.evidence_claim: A City document describes the Redlands Bowl as an amphitheater used for music and theatrical performances offered to the public without admission charge.
cards.source_title: Redlands Bowl Tile Roofing — City of Redlands
cards.access_notes: The source describes no-admission public performances; consult the current program before attending.

cards.title: Contemporary Club
cards.subtitle: Eureka Street corridor, 173 S. Eureka St.
cards.notes: Walk the Eureka Street block to see the Contemporary Club, then look for public library or city co-sponsored programs there.
cards.short_summary: A named civic event venue that hosts public programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s 2026 community calendar lists a free public concert at the Contemporary Club, 173 S. Eureka Street.
cards.source_title: Pianos Plus Free Concert — Redlands Community Calendar
cards.access_notes: The cited concert was free and public; future events and entry terms vary.

cards.title: First Congregational Church
cards.subtitle: Olive Avenue corridor, 2 W. Olive Ave.
cards.notes: Follow Olive Avenue from Cajon Street to view the surviving 1899 church building identified in the City’s historic context.
cards.short_summary: A documented 1899 building at Cajon and Olive.
cards.evidence_claim: The City historic-context statement says the First Congregational Church at 2 W. Olive Avenue, designed in 1899, still stands.
cards.access_notes: View from public sidewalks; enter only when the church is open to visitors or for an event.

cards.title: Ed Hales Park
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor, at Fifth and State streets
cards.notes: Use the State Street corridor to find the park at Fifth Street and check city listings for seasonal public gatherings.
cards.short_summary: A downtown park at a clearly identified State Street corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The City places Ed Hales Park at the corner of Fifth and State streets in Historic Downtown Redlands.
cards.source_title: Hotel Transylvania 3 at Movies in Park — City of Redlands
cards.access_notes: The City has used the park for free community programming; check current city event notices.

cards.title: Santa Fe Depot
cards.subtitle: Orange Street corridor, 347 Orange St.
cards.notes: Walk the Orange Street corridor to see the restored depot exterior and compare its 1910-era architecture with nearby downtown blocks.
cards.short_summary: A documented historic depot at a named Orange Street address.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists the Santa Fe Depot Rehabilitation/Restoration Project at 347 Orange Street.
cards.source_title: Current Development Projects — City of Redlands
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is appropriate; the cited City page identifies the restoration project and address.

cards.title: Redlands Post Office
cards.subtitle: State Street corridor, Historic Downtown Redlands
cards.notes: Include the State Street area in a self-guided architecture walk and identify the post office among the city’s documented historic buildings.
cards.short_summary: A downtown historic building on the National Register.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s planning document identifies the Redlands Post Office as a historic building listed on the National Register of Historic Places since 1985.
cards.source_title: Distinctive City — City of Redlands General Plan Background
cards.access_notes: View the building from public rights-of-way; postal-service access follows posted rules.
